# DRAFT FINDING — ⚠️ PROVISIONAL (pre-registered expectation, NOT a result)

*Generated by the results-watcher on 2026-07-09 during CS-independent prep. No real `outputs/ranked_perturbations.csv` exists yet. Every number below is either a **live database fact** (ChEMBL/ClinicalTrials, queried this pass) or a **pre-registered expectation** to be replaced by real analysis. Open Targets was rate-limited this pass; genetic calls are literature expectation pending OT confirmation.*

## Finding (provisional, ~180 words)

The pipeline ranks primary-human CD8⁺ T-cell CRISPR-KO perturbations by **causal effect size** (power-equalized E-distance, permutation-gated — not by p-value), filters for **viability** and **on-target knockdown**, treats **donors as replicates**, then applies a human-genetics **direction-of-effect concordance funnel** as the differentiator rather than the primary sort.

On the pre-registered expected hit set (SOCS1, CBLB, RASA2, TCEB2/ELOB, CD5, TNFAIP3, UBASH3A, ARID1A) the funnel is deliberately honest and sparse: **8 genes → 5 with any GWAS → 4 genome-wide-significant → 4 directional → 1 concordant.** The single strictly-concordant KO target is **UBASH3A** — the type-1-diabetes risk allele up-regulates UBASH3A, so loss-of-function is genetically *protective*; it is also novel and sits in a druggable histidine-phosphatase class, making it the **expected hero** (pending real effect sizes). **CBLB** is the tractability benchmark — two oral CBL-B inhibitors are already in trials (Nurix NX-1607; HotSpot HST-1011). **RASA2** is the highest-novelty, highest-risk play (undruggable, no genetics). Critically, the three best-genetics genes (SOCS1, CBLB, TNFAIP3) are `risk_lof`: mechanistically supportive but "discordant" under a strict cancer-anchored rule — showing concordance direction depends on the disease anchor.

## Expected hero vs. benchmarks (all provisional)

- **Hero (concordant + novel + tractable class): UBASH3A** — sole `protective_lof`; His-phosphatase handle; no existing program.
- **Positive control (validates the screen): CBLB** — clinically de-risked, strong autoimmune genetics.
- **Novelty play (high risk): RASA2** — Nature-2022 CAR-T persistence hit; undruggable, no directional genetics.
- **De-prioritized on safety/window:** TNFAIP3 (A20, lymphoma tumor-suppressor), ARID1A (tumor-suppressor), TCEB2/ELOB (likely pan-essential; its 100+ PDB structures are VHL/PROTAC scaffolds, not an ELOB pocket).

## 3-minute demo script (skeleton — provisional)

**0:00–0:30 — Problem & one-liner.** "Which T-cell perturbations *causally* improve effector function, and which are real drug targets? We rank by causal effect size, then keep only those with concordant human genetics."

**0:30–1:15 — Rigor (why judges should trust it).** Rank by E-distance not p (significance scales with cell count); viability gate (toxic/depleted KOs fail before ranking); on-target knockdown proof; donors as replicates via pseudobulk DE; fixed seeds + lockfile + one-command `make hero`.

**1:15–2:05 — The differentiator (live figure).** Walk the concordance funnel 8→5→4→4→1 from `concordance.py`. Make the honest point: concordance is *rare*, and direction depends on the disease anchor (risk_lof genes are brakes whose removal boosts immunity).

**2:05–2:40 — The nomination.** Expected hero **UBASH3A** (concordant, novel, druggable class) with **CBLB** as the positive control that proves the screen finds real biology (inhibitors already in the clinic). Propose the wet-lab test: opposite-modality replication (Schmidt 2022 CRISPRa should move the effector program the *opposite* way).

**2:40–3:00 — Provenance & ask.** Human-in-the-loop, per-stage artifacts, OSS-licensed, reproducible. Ask = the one slide that shows a novel, genetically-concordant, tractable target nominated end-to-end.

> ⚠️ Before demo: replace expectations with the real E-distance ranking + OT-confirmed directions. If the real top-10 differs from this pre-registered set, the funnel and hero must be recomputed — the *method* is the deliverable, not this specific list.
